items.prompt: What does ー mean in katakana words?
items.explanation: ー is not a kana and has no sound of its own: it makes the vowel before it long, held for about twice as long. コーヒー is kō-hī, not ko-hi. In vertical writing it turns into a vertical line. Vowel length changes meaning in Japanese, so the mark matters.
items.mnemonic: A long line for a long sound.
items.culture_note: Hiragana words show long vowels by adding a vowel kana instead, as in おかあさん (okāsan, mother); ー is used mainly in katakana.
